items.title: 台北選戰：蔣萬安的2028前哨戰，沈伯洋能否靠「洋流」突圍？
items.description: 原先不被看好的沈伯洋，自宣布參選後大力改變形象，近期聲勢高漲，給本享有執政優勢的蔣萬安帶來了挑戰。
items.content:
台北市長選戰：蔣萬安的2028前哨戰，沈伯洋能否靠「洋流」突圍？
  - Author, 蔣曜宇
  - Role, BBC中文特約記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 5 分鐘
台灣的「九合一」地方選舉將於11月28日舉行。
這場選舉將奠定執政的民進黨及在野的國民黨、民眾黨之間的勢力消長，不僅被視為是總統賴清德的「期中考」，更是2028總統大選的前哨戰。
外界密切關注俗稱「六都」的六個直轄市的選情。在首都台北，尋求連任的國民黨籍現任市長蔣萬安，被視作2028年總統大選的熱門人選之一，這次選戰打得是否漂亮，是他進一步問鼎中央的關鍵。
政治大學選舉研究中心研究員蔡佳泓對BBC中文分析：「2028年民進黨會由賴清德競選連任，這是蠻確定的事情。那重點就在國民黨。他們狀況還不是很明朗，可能人選有蔣萬安、盧秀燕、可能再加上鄭麗文，有很多的說法。這也讓大家更關注台北的選情。」
然而，原先不被看好的民進黨籍候選人、現任立委沈伯洋，自宣布參選後大力改變形象，並從9月開始聲勢高漲，其競選團隊以「洋流」為號招炒熱選情，給本享有執政優勢的蔣萬安帶來了挑戰。過去對選戰採取冷處理策略的蔣萬安團隊，也開始積極進行攻防，使台北選戰白熱化。
蔣萬安是誰？
今年47歲的蔣萬安，被視為2028年、甚至2032年總統大選的熱門人選之一。
蔣萬安在台北成長，畢業於國立政治大學法律系，隨後赴美取得美國賓州大學法學博士，在美國作為執業律師直到2013年返台。回台灣後，蔣萬安致力於幫助台灣新創產業在矽谷做募資、併購及上市的諮詢。
2015年，他放棄美國綠卡，以政治素人身份投入2016年立委選舉並成功當選，正式踏入政壇。當時國民黨因太陽花學運而受挫，蔣萬安為該黨帶來新氣象，隔年即高票當選國民黨中常委，成為黨內的政治明星。
2022年地方選舉，他擊敗對手陳時中、黃珊珊等人，當選台北市市長，以43歲之齡成為歷任最年輕市長。
兩岸立場方面，2019年蔣萬安擔任立委期間表示，認同總統蔡英文提出的「四個必須」，尤其是要對岸正視中華民國存在的事實；但他不能接受蔡英文「台灣從未接受九二共識」的說法。同年香港爆發反送中運動，他在臉書發文聲援香港示威者，並稱一國兩制在台灣沒有存在的空間。
在市長任內，他推動兩岸穩定交流，曾兩度赴上海參加上海台北雙城論壇，也在台北接待上海市府訪團。他批評民進黨政府「逢中必反」的立場，呼籲儘快恢復兩岸觀光和人員往來。
近年來，蔣萬安在多個場合強調，兩岸關係越緊張，越需要溝通與交流。但他也迴避提及「九二共識」與「兩岸一家親」等政治意涵較高的口號。
在市政層面，蔣萬安就任三週年時表示，他最自豪的政績包含台北大巨蛋的啟用、捷運工程開發，以及修法協調讓美國晶片大廠輝達（Nvidia）台灣總部成功落腳台北。後者將投入新台幣400億資金，預估帶動超過一萬個工作機會。
值得留意的是，蔣萬安2019年擔任立委期間，在同婚法案中投下贊同票，是少數公開支持婚姻平權的國民黨立委，他擔任市長後也曾公開參加台北彩虹遊行。這次選舉前夕，台北市警察10月3日突擊搜索一間同志酒吧，引發性平團體批評及上百民眾抗議，蔣萬安作為市長的回應備受關注。
台北市一般被認為是藍營大本營，在這次選舉前期他也大幅領先對手。據TVBS民調中心5月報告，蔣萬安獲得58%的支持度，而沈伯洋只有30%；但信民協會最新9月民調卻顯示兩人差距已縮小到1.2%，使台北選情升溫。
對支持者而言，蔣萬安是一個非傳統的國民黨政治人物。他清新、溫和的首都市長人設，讓他在藍大於綠的台北市更容易鞏固基本盤並吸引中間選民。其反對者則批評蔣萬安為「背稿機」，在公開演說方面缺乏群眾魅力。
個人生活方面，蔣萬安的身世一直備受討論。2005年，蔣萬安的父親、前總統府秘書長蔣孝嚴，透過多方文獻佐證自己為蔣經國的私生子，並將姓氏從「章」改為「蔣」，蔣萬安也因此隨父改姓。
蔣萬安曾在自傳中提到，雖然從小就聽過耳語，但他是到高中才從父親那得知自己與蔣家的關聯，稱他們之間有「切不斷的血緣關係」。蔣家第四代蔣友青則公開質疑蔣萬安從未與他們進行DNA鑑定。
蔣萬安與妻子育有三子。近期，其15歲的長子錄取台北市教育局的公費赴美交換計畫，引發輿論質疑市長是否利用特權且未主動利益迴避。蔣萬安對外說明，自己並無介入孩子的甄選過程，但也表示不會領取教育局的新台幣7.5萬元補助金。
沈伯洋是誰？
今年44歲的沈伯洋，為目前台灣政壇上群眾反應最極化的政治人物之一。
綠營支持者稱讚他論述清晰且具國際觀，認為他提升了台灣社會的防衛意識，是「抗中保台」的指標性人物；泛藍選民則指他頻繁將國內政治攻防歸咎於「中共統戰」，並認為他所推動的民防運動是在販賣焦慮，視之為激進派。
沈伯洋在台北出生長大，畢業於台大法律學系，考上法律學研究所後曾以「撲馬」為藝名任職補習班多年，專門教授刑法。他2007年赴美留學，取得賓州大學法學碩士及加州大學爾灣分校犯罪學與法律社會學博士學位，2017年放棄美國教職返台，任教於國立台北大學犯罪學研究所，研究中國對台統戰及威脅。
他在2021年創辦提倡全民防衛的「黑熊學院」，並曾在分析中國資訊戰的台灣民主實驗室擔任理事長，是國際研討會上的常客。
2024年，沈伯洋在立委選舉中以不分區排名第二，成為民進黨籍立委，正式步入政壇。在他當上立委的同一年，北京稱他為「台獨頑固分子」並加以制裁。
沈伯洋對中國大陸的強硬態度，使他捲入多起爭議。
他曾表示，陸配參政前需明確放棄中國國籍，否則可能衍生國安危機，是要防範的「緊急事態」。國民黨和反對者稱其打壓陸配參政權，使陸配被歧視。
中國國台辦曾制裁沈伯洋父親沈土城的貿易公司，稱他與中國企業有商業往來。沈伯洋則對外表示，該指控為中國「認知作戰」的一環，指父親公司主要在中南美洲做貿易，中國只是多個進口來源之一。
2025年「大罷免」，民進黨中央以「罷免投同意，反共更有力」作為號召，沈伯洋被視為這場運動的核心領軍人物之一，反對罷免陣營批評他煽動社會對立。最終32起罷免案全數不通過，沈伯洋表示會負起責任，但稱罷免團體為自主集結，不該因行使公民權利而被苛責。
大罷免後的同年10月底，中國重慶市公安局以涉嫌「分裂國家」為由對沈伯洋發布通緝令。中國官媒央視其後播出一段7分鐘紀錄片，指控沈伯洋傳播「仇中」思想，其創辦的「黑熊學院」三年內訓練逾300萬名「黑熊勇士」協助防衛台灣。沈伯洋回應指，中國無權在台灣行使司法管轄，自己絕不退縮。
沈伯洋過去因推動「抗中保台」等被反對者認為「高仇恨值」，他自宣布參選台北市長後大力改變形象，首先剪去原本標誌性的爆炸頭，並將論述重點從國防與兩岸轉換到市政治理等社會議題，積極跑基層來彌補地方經營上的不足。其論述能力為他帶來聲量，外界關注他是否「破圈」取得非同溫層支持者。
不過，遭對岸通緝的沈伯洋始終離不開兩岸議題。近期被追問對雙城論壇的看法時，他表示若當選，將重新評估雙城論壇的效益，主張台北應與更多國際都市交流，不應限縮在兩岸之間。他強調，只要無政治前提，他不排斥赴對岸交流，問題在對方要不要讓他進去。
10月4日，沈伯洋舉行競選總部成立大會，主辦單位稱有超過12萬人參與，包含在兩岸享有高知名度的主持人蔡康永。中國大陸網民強烈反應，「蔡康永現身台獨份子競選會場」一度登上微博熱搜榜第一，曾合作的大陸品牌零跑汽車下架其代言廣告。
外界原本預期沈伯洋勝選機率低，但隨著選情白熱化，他與對手間的差距逐漸縮小。
台灣中央研究院政治學研究所研究員鮑彤（Nathan F. Batto）撰文指出，沈伯洋並沒有照劇本演出他被分派的那個「毫無勝算、注定落敗」的角色。相反，他掌握了整個選戰的節奏，使蔣萬安團隊捉襟見肘。
「事情本來不應該這樣發展的。但台北選戰卻出人意料地變得非常有趣。」鮑彤寫道。

items.title: 俄羅斯鼠疫實驗室人員死亡 美方稱「密切關注」
items.description: 鼠疫桿菌，又稱耶爾森氏鼠疫桿菌（Yersinia pestis）曾在 14 世紀導致歐洲一半人口死亡，當時被稱為黑死病。最近而該地區的囓齒動物（如土撥鼠）中就發現了這種細菌。
items.content:
俄羅斯鼠疫實驗室人員死亡 美方稱「密切關注」
  - Author, 派崔克·傑克遜 （Patrick Jackson）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
美國總統特朗普（Donald Trump 川普）表示，美國正在「非常密切地」關註一名俄羅斯實驗室技術員在西伯利亞一家鼠疫研究中心死亡的案件。
國務卿馬可·盧比奧（Marco Rubio 魯比奧）表示，華盛頓正在密切關注事態發展，擔心該事件可能導致肺鼠疫的傳播，但目前沒有理由感到恐慌。
俄羅斯伊爾庫茨克州長（Irkutsk）稱死因是「病因不明的肺炎」，並表示「在死者的生物樣本中沒有發現與該女子工作有關的微生物」。
未經證實的消息指出，該名女子是在打破盛裝病原體的試管後生病，也可能是在前往一個鼠疫在野生齧齒動物中自然流行的地區進行野外考察後發病。
當被問及華盛頓將如何應對瘟疫從俄羅斯擴散的風險時，特朗普稱他尚未就此與克里姆林宮進行溝通。
「我很遺憾看到他們遇到這種情況，」特朗普說，他又補充道：「我們會幫忙的。凡是遇到這類問題的人，我們都會盡力幫助。」
伊爾庫茨克州長伊戈爾·科布澤夫（Igor Kobzev）援引俄羅斯消費者權益和健康監督機構 （Rospotrebnadzor）聲明說，自該實驗室技術員死亡以來，尚未有其他來自鼠疫研究所的工作人員尋求醫療救助的報告。
該監管機構又稱，生物安全小組已對位於伊爾庫茨克的西伯利亞和遠東防鼠疫研究所進行了檢查，並未發現緊急情況。
對此，克里姆林宮發言人德米特里·佩斯科夫（Dmitry Peskov）敦促人們不要「聽信各種謠言」，而應該「相信俄羅斯消費者權益保護和福利監督局的官方聲明。」
俄羅斯媒體上週報道稱，近200名已知與死者有接觸的人正在接受醫學觀察，以防萬一。
當記者詢問「俄羅斯疑似鼠疫病例的最新情況」時，盧比奧說：「似乎實驗室裡有一名工作人員被感染了，人們擔心這可能會傳播開來，至少在內部擴散——你已經看到他們有採取隔離行動。」
「如果這類病毒傳播出去，速度會非常快。因此我們正密切關注和監控。我認為這並不值得恐慌，但確實需要我們重視並密切關注，而我們也正在這樣做。」
根據俄羅斯媒體報道，這名已過世的女子名叫達莉亞（Daria），年近30，她最近曾造訪過與蒙古國接壤的布里亞特地區（Buryatia）。
100多年前，為了回應1920年代爆發的鼠疫，西伯利亞和遠東抗鼠疫研究所成立了。
英國雷丁大學（ University of Reading）細胞微生物學副教授克拉克博士（Simon Clarke）告訴 BBC 廣播4台的節目稱，鼠疫耶爾森病毒引起的肺鼠疫如果不及時治療幾乎總是致命的，但可以用抗生素治療。
「肺鼠疫可透過人與人之間的接觸傳播，這就是人們對此感到擔憂的原因，」他說。
他又補充強調：「但當然，人們一想到傳染病爆發，首先想到的就是……封鎖和新冠疫情，但這在這裡根本不會發生。」
克拉克說：「人們認為：哦！瘟疫已經過去了，幾百年前就過去了，但事實並非如此。」
「它仍然存在，在世界某些地區，它對人類健康構成威脅，這就是為什麼他們需要研究它。」
當被問及這種病原體是否有可能被研究用於生物武器時，這位科學家承認這是可能的。
克拉克博士說：「因為是俄羅斯，人們自然而然會想到這一點，但我認為我之前的解釋可能更合理」。
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。

items.title: 美國圖書館為何正迅速下架眾多圖書？
items.description: 美國公共圖書館已成為一場激烈意識形態衝突的戰場，這場衝突的焦點在於學生應該能夠獲得哪些書籍。
items.content:
美國圖書館為何正迅速下架眾多圖書？
  - Author, 聖地亞哥·瓦內加斯（Santiago Vanegas）
  - Role, BBC西班牙語世界網（BBC News Mundo）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 5 分鐘
五年前，居住在美國佛羅里達州皮內拉斯縣（Pinellas County, Florida）的一位母親妮可（Nicole）注意到，她孩子學校裡的某些書籍被移除了。
她的孩子們自己也注意到有些書已經找不到了，她透過與老師和圖書管理員交談證實了這一點。
所以妮可決定給她的四個孩子買他們在學校裡找不到的書——她承認這種情況與大多數家庭的實際情況大相逕庭。
她說：「在我居住的地方，有些社區沒有額外的收入來購買書籍。」
她補充表示：「由於工作安排，照顧孩子的父母和祖父母無法帶孩子去圖書館。」
美國的公共圖書館已成為激烈意識形態辯論的戰場，參與辯論的有家長、教師、圖書館員、活動團體和政治家，他們爭論的焦點是兒童應該提供哪些書籍。
根據美國圖書館協會（ALA）知識自由辦公室統計，僅2025年一年，公共圖書館和學校圖書館就發生了6588起圖書審查事件——即圖書被完全下架或移至限制更嚴格的區域。
受影響的具體書目有4235種。
相較之下，2001年至 2020 年間，每年平均有70本書遭到審查。
密切關注此事的組織認為，實際數字可能要高得多，因為大家尚未注意這些書籍移除事件。
「從未有過這麼多的孩子，被剝奪了接觸這麼多故事的機會，」美國筆會（PEN America）的最新報告指出。該組織旨在捍衛言論自由並監督圖書審查制度。
這一增長恰逢數十項州級法律，甚至是一些聯邦措施的通過，旨在限制公立學校獲取被認為不合適的書籍。
「過去幾年我們看到的是一種截然不同的升級，」美國組織「全國反審查聯盟」（National Coalition Against Censorship）的詹馬爾科·安特斯卡（Gianmarco Antosca）向BBC解釋說。
「禁書現像已蔓延到學校之外。我們看到許多州甚至聯邦層面都出現了禁書立法。」
支持這些限制措施的組織以及促成這些限制的官員表示，他們的唯一目標是防止兒童接觸到不適合其年齡的內容。
他們還稱，這些限制是為了捍衛父母對其子女教育做出決定的權利。
「自由媽媽」（Moms for Liberty）是挑戰書籍內容最活躍的民間團體之一。
該組織拒絕了BBC的採訪，但其執行董事蒂娜·德斯科維奇（Tina Descovich）在一份聲明中說明：「（我們）致力於保護兒童免受學校圖書館中不適合其年齡的露骨性內容和意識形態材料的侵害。」
但是，誰該決定哪些書籍適合學校圖書館，以及如何決定呢？
書籍是如何被禁的
美國公立學校的禁書令在全國各地並不統一，也不總是遵循相同的程序。
例如，根據美國筆會的統計，在2024年至2025年期間，佛羅里達州和得克薩斯州發生了數百起圖書移除事件，而俄克拉荷馬州和新墨西哥州等則沒有記錄到此類事件。
將一本書從公立學校移除的過程，通常始於家長或其他社區成員認為該書不合適，並向當地教育部門提出正式反對意見。
一個值得注意的例子是佛州希爾斯伯勒縣（Hillsborough County, Florida），該縣是坦帕市（Tampa）的所在地。
2024年年中，當地媒體報導稱，兩名州高級官員曾致函希爾斯伯勒縣教育局長，要求其將他們認為「色情」的書籍從該縣學校移除。
隨後被下架的59本書中包括安德烈·艾席蒙（（André Aciman）的《以你的名字呼喚我》（Call Me by Your Name），雅·吉亞西（Yaa Gyasi）講述18世紀西非出生的兩姐妹及其後代故事的獲獎歷史小說《歸鄉》（Homecoming），以及《列王的紛爭》（A Clash of Kings）——該系列的第二部作品是熱門電視劇《權力的遊戲》（Game of Thrones）的靈感來源。
「自我審查」的影響
據美國筆會佛羅里達辦事處主任威廉·強森（William Johnson）稱，此案的影響遠遠超出了希爾斯伯勒縣。
在收到信件並質疑教育局長之後，「美國筆會記錄到，（除希爾斯伯勒學區外）至少有九個佛州學區在學年開始前，從教室和圖書館移走了數百本書」。
他告訴BBC：「這些學區面臨的是同樣的法律和政治環境，它們選擇撤回教材以避免州政府強制執行的風險，而不是等待傳統的複議程序進行。」
例如，據美國圖書館協會稱，包含性少數（LGBT+）角色或涉及性別、種族和性取向等問題的書籍更容易成為攻擊目標。
該協會還說明，2025年受到質疑的書籍中，有39%講述的是 LGBT+ 族群或少數群體成員的故事。
關於父母權利的辯論
一些保守組織採取了協調一致的行動，援引所謂的父母權利——對子女教育做出決定的權利——對書籍提出質疑並遊說將其下架。
美國「公民自由組織」（Citizens for Freedom）——一個積極參與此運動的團體——一份文件強調，是「父母」，而非政府或學校，擁有「上帝賦予的」權力來「撫養、教育和在道德上塑造他們的孩子」。
然而，關於家長是否真的是將書籍從學校和圖書館書架上移除的幕後推手，目前仍有爭議。
據美國圖書館協會知識自由辦公室指出，2025年，有92% 的「圖書挑戰」是由倡導團體和政府官員發起的。
「從來沒有證據表明這項努力是由目前就讀公立學校的家長發起的，」佛州閱讀自由計畫（Florida Freedom to Read Project, FFTRP）主任、兩個孩子都在橘郡（Orange County）公立學校就讀的母親斯蒂芬娜·費雷爾（Stephana Ferrell）說。
她向BBC補充：「從一開始，這場運動就是由與公立學校聯繫甚少的特殊利益集團領導的。」
禁書的代價
妮可是一位住在皮內拉斯縣，育有四個孩子的母親，她告訴BBC，正是因為她相信父母的權利，所以她反對學校禁書。
「通過禁書，你是在為其他孩子做決定，而不是為你的孩子做決定。」
妮可嬙調，作為一名讀者和一位母親，她對學校禁書最感到遺憾的是，「你奪走了別人的鏡子，奪走了別人的窗戶，奪走了別人批判性思考自己所處世界的能力」。
2023年，前總統拜登的政府發起了一系列舉措，調查公立學校日益增多的禁書趨勢，並勸阻各學區限制學生接觸有爭議的書籍。
但特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）總統去年年初上任後不久，教育部駁回了現有的投訴，稱這種現像是騙局，並辯稱被移除的書籍「不適合兒童年齡、包含露骨的性內容或淫穢內容」。
共和黨議員提出的一項法案目前正在美國國會審議中。
該法案威脅要對「向18歲以下兒童提供或推廣包含性內容的文學作品或其他材料」的學校，扣留其資金。
對於佛州閱讀自由計畫的費雷爾來說，美國禁書現像日益增多的最嚴重後果是「人們默默接受了圖書館、文學和閱讀自由不再值得捍衛這一事實」。
她總結說：「當那些有權保護這些自由的人反而選擇放棄這些自由時，損失遠遠超出了書籍本身。」

items.title: 中美AI軍事化背景下 BBC獲悉五角大樓正式停用 Anthropic 工具
items.description: 今年2月，五角大樓將 Anthropic 列為「供應鏈風險」，此前該公司拒絕移除其工具中的安全防護機制。
items.content:
中美AI軍事化背景下 BBC獲悉五角大樓正式停用 Anthropic 工具
  - Author, 卡莉·海斯（Kali Hays）
  - Role, BBC科技記者
  - Reporting from, 舊金山（三藩市）報導
  - Author, 丹尼爾·布什（Daniel Bush）
  - Role, BBC駐華盛頓記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
一名官員向BBC透露，美國國防部已不再使用 Anthropic 的人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧）工具。數月前，五角大樓以國家安全為由，將該公司列為供應鏈風險。
這名國防部官員在週一（10月5日）的一份聲明中表示，五角大樓（The Pentagon）「已停止使用 Anthropic 的產品」。
國防部長赫格塞斯今年2月將 Anthropic 列為供應鏈風險，並宣布五角大樓將在8月下旬前停用其產品。目前尚不清楚為何出現延誤。
多名知情人士告訴BBC，直到上週，該部門仍在研究、分析、情報蒐集以及針對伊朗的軍事行動中使用 Anthropic 的 Claude 模型。
知情人士稱，Claude 被視為梳理海量信息的關鍵工具。他們包括曾與五角大樓在人工智能領域密切合作的前美國國防官員和承包商。
BBC就五角大樓的聲明向 Anthropic 求證，該公司發言人拒絕置評。
國防部全面停用 Anthropic 工具的細節此前未見報道。
自2024年起，Anthropic 的產品一直被美國政府和軍方使用，它也是首家工具被部署到涉密政府機構的先進 AI 公司。
但今年早些時候，五角大樓向該公司施壓，要求移除 Claude 的安全護欄，讓軍方不受限制地使用其 AI 產品。
Anthropic 以對大規模監控和自主武器的擔憂為由拒絕。赫格塞斯隨後將該公司列為「國家安全供應鏈風險」——這一法律手段通常只用於總部位於對美國構成威脅國家的企業。
Anthropic 稱此舉「史無前例且違法」，並已起訴特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）政府，試圖推翻這一認定。
在這場法律訴訟推進的同時，五角大樓與谷歌（Google）、xAI 和 OpenAI 等其他大型科技公司簽署了合同。
據兩名熟悉國防部 AI 使用情況的人士透露，近幾個月來，OpenAI 的工具在部分軍事部門得到了更廣泛的應用。
五角大樓週一的聲明，是回應BBC關於其使用 Anthropic 產品的提問。此前多名受訪者表示，Claude 仍在被廣泛使用。
多名消息人士稱，Claude 被嵌入五角大樓使用的一個更大的數據平台——Maven 智能系統（Maven Smart System）。
Maven 由帕蘭提爾（Palantir）運營，是五角大樓整合情報和其他數據的主要平台。
喬治城大學（Georgetown University）安全與新興技術研究中心高級研究分析師勞倫·卡恩（Lauren Kahn）表示，由於 Claude 已深度嵌入 Maven，要迅速將其從系統中移除並不容易。
「五角大樓直到現在才把Claude從整個系統中全部移除，這說明這類系統並非即插即用，」她說。
「一旦它們被整合進去，再想剝離就會很痛苦，」曾任美國國防官員的卡恩補充道。
BBC採訪了專門從事 AI 業務、與五角大樓密切合作的國防承包商，以及前美國國防官員和其他熟悉五角大樓人工智能應用情況的人士。其中數人因未獲授權向媒體發聲而要求匿名。
一名前美國國防部高級官員表示，當赫格塞斯最初下令在政府部門逐步淘汰 Anthropic 時，「外界曾擔心從 Anthropic 轉向 OpenAI」及其他工具是否順利。
2月27日，赫格塞斯下達了六個月內淘汰 Anthropic 的最後期限，次日美國和以色列即對伊朗發動襲擊。
一名知情人士稱，在與該公司爭議的「整個過程中」，五角大樓員工一直在使用 Anthropic 的 Claude 工具，包括其強大的 Mythos 模型。
多名消息人士稱，Claude 被特別用於情報蒐集和分析，包括通過帕蘭提爾的 Maven 系統。帕蘭提爾是一家領先的國防技術公司，由總統唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump）的億萬富翁盟友彼得·蒂爾（Peter Thiel）創辦。
熟悉該技術應用方式的消息人士稱，分析人員和其他國防官員依靠 Maven 獲取和整理可視化數據，包括衛星圖像和無人機影像。
這些數據隨後被輸入 Claude 和其他大語言模型，用於識別潛在軍事目標等任務。
一名今年年初曾獲帕蘭提爾演示 Maven 的消息人士稱，官員們在編寫上報指揮鏈的一頁紙簡報時經常使用這項技術。
部分美國盟友也使用 Maven 與特朗普政府共享情報。
Anthropic 與五角大樓的衝突發生之際，該公司與白宮的關係似乎正在回暖。上週，特朗普在白宮兩次會見了 Anthropic 掌門人阿莫迪。
在其中一次與特朗普及其他科技界領袖的會晤後，阿莫迪表示他仍然擔憂 AI 帶來的風險。
「如何應對這些風險仍在討論之中，」阿莫迪在白宮對記者說，特朗普就站在他身旁，「但如果我們與總統合作，我們就能安全地取勝。」
特朗普隨後稱讚了阿莫迪，稱他「很了不起」、「非常棒」。
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。
背景：AI軍備競賽，中國的步伐和影響
BBC中文記者陳岩
五角大樓停用 Anthropic，不代表美軍退出 AI 軍事競賽。爭議的核心在於：軍方與科技公司之間，誰有權決定技術如何使用。Anthropic 拒絕放棄對大規模國內監控和全自主武器的限制，美國國防部則要求接受「任何合法用途」。
這也不是一家反對軍事用途的 AI 公司與軍方的對抗。Anthropic 表明，支持將 AI 用於合法的境外情報與反情報任務。消息人士在2月份向BBC透露，Anthropic 的大模型 Claude 曾被用於美國抓捕委內瑞拉總統尼古拉斯·馬杜羅（Nicolás Maduro）的行動。
相比之下，AI 在伊朗戰事中的角色更清晰。帕蘭提爾英國暨歐洲區負責人路易斯·莫斯利（Louis Mosley）4月份接受BBC專訪時稱，其 Maven 智能系統（Maven Smart System）在作戰管理中「起了作用」。
據報導，Maven 智能系統做到了匯集情報、衛星圖像與無人機影像，分析後提出打擊目標建議，還能按可用兵力和裝備，建議動用何種程度的武力。而 Claude 正是支撐該系統的 AI 大模型之一。
雖然帕蘭提爾強調，最終決定仍由人作出。但受訪專家向BBC表示，一旦速度和打擊規模成為優先考量，軍人未必有足夠時間核查目標，甚至可能過度依賴軟件的判斷。爭議因此不止於「是否有人按下按鈕」，更在於操作者能否真正理解並審查 AI 的建議。
這場爭議的大背景，依然是與中國的競爭。美國人工智能國家安全委員會（National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence）曾反對全面禁止 AI 驅動的自主武器，並警告，若中國率先部署 AI 驅動的蜂群無人機系統，美國可能失去軍事技術優勢。批評者則認為，這類主張可能助長一場不負責任的軍備競賽。
今年2月，美國國防部副部長埃米爾·邁克爾（Emil Michael）被問及五角大樓為何不接納 Anthropic 的合同限制時說：「我們確實必須為中國正在做的事情做好準備。」
有限的報道也揭示出中國的努力。路透社2024年根據研究論文稱，包括解放軍軍事科學院下屬機構研究人員在內的團隊，利用 Meta 公開發布的早期 Llama 模型，開發出名為 ChatBIT 的工具，研究其在情報處理和作戰決策支援方面的用途。
另一條路徑是無人裝備。2025年九三閱兵中，中國展示了多種無人系統，涵蓋無人潛航器、無人機及「機器狼」。
競爭之外，中美也曾劃出共同底線。2024年11月，習近平與時任美國總統拜登（Joe Biden）達成共識：動用核武器的決定必須由人類掌控，不能交給 AI。但這並非針對所有軍事 AI 的禁令，也未釐清常規武器、情報分析與目標識別的使用邊界。
而在特朗普第二任期，即便是上述共識，是否還存在，也被打上了問號。儘管兩人關係有所改善，但特朗普已多次明確表示，不打算對 AI 發展施加任何限制。
Anthropic 事件凸顯的，正是 AI 軍事化邊界的模糊：政府以應對競爭對手為由，要求更大的使用權限；企業則試圖守住限制。即便最終決定仍由人作出，如何避免人在高速決策中淪為 AI 建議的「批准者」，仍是軍方與技術供應商繞不開的問題。

items.title: 駐日美軍涉謀殺女性被捕 重燃沖繩抗議浪潮
items.description: 對於沖繩島上的許多當地人來說，再次有駐日美軍涉嫌犯罪被捕，喚起了他們數十年來積累的挫折感。
items.content:
「又來了」：美國海軍陸戰隊員涉謀殺女性被捕 重燃日本沖繩抗議浪潮
  - Author, 森來實（Kurumi Mori）
  - Role, BBC駐日本記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
對許多沖繩居民而言，一名美軍士兵被控在酒店房間內搶劫並殺害一名女子後被捕，再次點燃了他們數十年來對當地涉及美軍人員犯罪事件的不滿。
長期居住在沖繩，52歲的佐藤愛（Ai Sato；音譯）對BBC說：「老實說，我的第一反應是：『怎麼又來了？』」
「從我小時候到現在，甚麼都沒有改變。我們究竟還要重演多少次同樣的事情，製造更多受害者，令他們的家人承受痛苦，最終讓沖繩人民陷入悲傷？」
居住在宜野灣市，62歲的大城明美（Akemi Oshiro；音譯）也有相同感受。
她向BBC表示：「我知道我們不應該對這種可怕的事情習以為常，但它們一再發生，我已經不再感到驚訝。」
沖繩擁有日本規模最大的美軍駐紮力量，設有多個美軍基地，並駐有數以萬計的美軍人員。
二十歲的美國海軍陸戰隊下士德文·雅各布·巴拉德（L/Cpl Devin Jacob Ballard）星期日（10月4日）被日本警察逮捕。警方表示，調查仍在進行中，由於涉嫌罪行與官方軍務無關，因此巴拉德目前由日本當局拘留。
美軍人員當時是否正在執行官方職務，將決定哪個國家擁有主要司法管轄權。當日本擁有管轄權、但疑犯由美方羈押時，美方可在日本正式起訴前繼續保留羈押權。
巴拉德隸屬第三海軍陸戰隊遠征軍（III Marine Expeditionary Force），駐紮於宜野灣市的普天間海軍陸戰隊航空基地。
沖繩縣警察表示，39歲的屋宜杏奈（Anna Yagi）於3日凌晨被發現陳屍於那霸市一間酒店房間內。
據稱，閉路電視畫面顯示，一名相信是疑犯的男子與該名女子一同進入酒店，其後獨自離開，並帶走她的財物。當地媒體引述警方報導稱，屋宜似乎被繩索勒頸致死。
日本首相高市早苗已向華盛頓提出正式抗議。但像佐藤這樣的居民認為，這遠遠不足夠。
「我對政府數十年來一再發表同樣的評論感到非常失望，例如表示會提出抗議，或稱高度重視這宗事件。」
她說：「我希望高市首相直接致電特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）總統。她一直強調自己與特朗普關係密切，我希望她能與他討論具體措施，防止同類事件再次發生。」
涉嫌謀殺案的消息傳出後，日本各地民眾表達憤怒情緒，約100人分別在那霸及東京舉行抗議活動。另有不少人透過社交媒體表達憤怒並要求伸張正義，其中一名用戶寫道：「夠了。」
過去幾年，多宗事故及罪案令當地反對美軍繼續駐紮沖繩的聲音日益高漲。
2016年，一名20歲沖繩女子遭強姦及殺害後，數以萬計示威者走上街頭，抗議當地龐大的美軍駐紮規模。涉案的一名前美國海軍陸戰隊員其後被判終身監禁。
目前約有5.5萬名美軍人員駐紮日本，其中最集中駐紮於這個亞熱帶群島。沖繩雖然是日本面積最小的縣份之一，但日本境內專供美軍使用土地的70%位於沖繩。
1972年，在美軍於第二次世界大戰結束後佔領沖繩群島多年後，沖繩縣重新回歸日本管治。沖繩縣政府資料顯示，自那時起，已錄得6,409宗涉及美軍人員的刑事拘捕。
當地居民表示，大規模美軍駐紮引發多方面不滿，問題包括強姦、襲擊及酒後駕駛事故等罪案，以及噪音和軍機墜毀等對社區造成的滋擾。
1995年，三名美軍士兵在一名12歲女學生從文具店步行回家途中將她綁架、毆打及強姦。
2025年，一名美國海軍陸戰隊員因勒頸及性侵一名日本女子而被定罪。
育有兩名兒子、48歲的宮城瞳（Hitomi Miyagi；音譯）向BBC表示：「戰爭結束80年後，我們居住的沖繩仍然是一個令人惶惶不安的地方。」
「我們不會停止發聲，希望迎來一個能夠和平生活的沖繩。」

items.title: 德国首位AfD州议长：劳施当选萨安州议长
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德国首位afd州议长：劳施当选萨安州议长/a-79565827?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 劳施成为萨克森-安哈尔特州议长。35岁的他在第一轮选举中当选该州议会的这一最高职务。由此，德国首次出现选择党（AfD）籍的州议长。
items.content:
德国首次出现选择党籍州议长：劳施当选萨安州议长
2026年10月6日
（德国之声中文网）德国首次选出一位选择党（AfD）州议会议长。35岁的劳施（Tobias Rausch）当选萨克森-安哈尔特州议长。周二（10月6日），劳施在马格德堡的州议会获得了48票支持，达到了必要的多数。
劳施目前担任萨安州议会选择党团幕僚长以及选择党在该州的秘书长。除了本党的议席以外，还有9名选择党以外的议员给劳施投了赞成票。而事先已官宣支持劳施的萨安州议会BSW党团有五个议席。这意味着，还有四个赞成票来自选择党和BSW之外。
据德国电视一台报道，由于是不公开计票，不清楚劳施还获得了哪个阵营的支持。基民盟党团主席团此前建议其15名议员投弃权票。社民党、绿党和左翼党各自拥有8个议席，此前表示反对投票给劳施。
在当选后的致辞中，劳施希望扫除对他任职的顾虑。“我不会成为某个党团的议长，而是整个萨安州议会的议长。”
广泛的职权范围
德国电视一台报道说，州议长的职权范围相当广泛：主持会议、要求与会者遵守秩序、邀请国宾，并拥有州议会所在建筑的管理权。此外，州议长还有对州议会行政部门的人事权。
劳施被视为选择党首席竞选者西格蒙德（Ulrich Siegmund）多年的同路人。今年初，劳施是受到裙带关系指控的选择党政客之一。劳施的多个兄弟姊妹曾在一段时间内受聘于一名联邦议员。劳施则表示，他未参与这些雇佣事宜。
德国电视一台报道说，在州议会首次会议上，萨安州州长的选举未列入议程。选择党的获胜者西格蒙德此前宣布，将于12月参选。他表示，能获得必要的多数，尽管尚无其它政党愿与该党联合执政。在新选举完成以前，现任基民盟州长舒尔茨（Sven Schulze）继续留任。
今年9月6日，选择党在萨安州议会选举中以43.8%的得票率获胜，但未获得绝对多数。德国宪法保护部门将萨安州选择党定性为已确认的右翼极端主义。

items.title: 德语媒体：难以奏效的“威慑武器”
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：难以奏效的-威慑武器/a-79565894?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 德法两国建议，欧盟今后遭遇经济胁迫时，将有权禁止相关国家进入欧盟统一市场。《南德意志报》评论称，这一建议本身就意味着欧盟对华贸易政策正在转向强硬。《法兰克福汇报》则认为，这种威慑只是一厢情愿，因为北京能够承受失去欧洲市场的冲击，但稀土断供却足以令欧洲工业立即停摆。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）《南德意志报》评论写道，为防止随时可能爆发的贸易战，德法两国建议欧盟应准备一款强有力的施压工具，以便迅速而有效地应对来自中国等国的经济胁迫。例如，当相关国家发出禁止出口关键原材料的威胁时，欧盟就有权禁止该国部分乃至所有企业进入欧盟统一市场。尽管德法两国并没有直接点名，但矛头所指显然就是中国。这篇题为《欧盟不再客气》 的评论写道：
“为了本国的政治和经济利益，中国及其他一些国家可谓无所不用其极，而德法两国就是在这一背景下提出上述计划的。多年以来，德国一直反对欧盟对中国采取激进措施，因为德国担心汽车等工业产品的对华出口会因此受到影响。但现如今，德国总理府已经越来越意识到，北京正在日益频繁地将其经济实力当作政治施压手段，而为了避免德国的工业基础被进一步掏空，德国必须予以回击。
除此之外，柏林还意识到，中欧贸易冲突中，欧盟的处境远比想象中要好：的确，欧盟的很多原材料都高度依赖从中国进口，因为中国是少数或仅有的出产国。但另一方面，受中国内需疲软和中美贸易战的影响，对许多中国企业来说，欧盟已经成了不可或缺的销售市场。而德国总理默茨和法国总统马克龙就是希望充分利用欧盟的这一有利地位。
一段时间以来，欧盟对华贸易的逆差已经高达每天十亿欧元，而且仍在继续扩大。今天，已经没有任何一个欧盟成员国的对华贸易保持顺差。中国将高额补贴后的过剩产品以倾销价抛向国际市场。‘中国冲击’之下，汽车、机械制造以及化工等德国工业核心无一幸免。”
《南德意志报》的评论指出，在谈论德法联合提议的新工具时，联邦政府官员使用了源自冷战核威慑战略的“二次打击武器”一词，这足以表明国际贸易争执的激烈程度。而这场争执很有可能会在今年秋季迎来摊牌时刻：
 
“本周，欧盟贸易专员谢夫乔维奇（Maroš Šefčovič）将在北京同中国商务部长王文涛举行会谈。今年六月以来。中欧双方一直在讨论如何消除双边贸易关系中日益严重的失衡问题，但迄今一直未能取得成果。
私下里，欧盟委员会内部一致认为，此次谢夫乔维奇的北京之行也将无功而返。有鉴于此，支持进一步限制对华贸易的欧盟国家将占据多数。一般认为，王文涛不会满足欧盟有关中国自愿减少部分行业对欧出口的愿望。
欧盟筹建新武器的同时，德法两国还希望欧盟现有政策工具也能得到进一步的强化，例如反倾销措施以及为单一国家设立进口上限等等。”
缺乏可信度的“核选项”
《法兰克福汇报》则认为，只要欧盟仍不能摆脱在稀土等关键原材料领域的对华依赖，德法提出的“二次打击武器”就无法产生威慑力量：
”尽管欧盟已拥有反胁迫工具，但迄今启动该工具却困难重重。默茨和马克龙希望改变这一现状，并赋予欧盟委员会自主启动新工具的权限，而成员国要想阻挠该工具的启动，则必须拥有多数。
 
但德法建议中也明确要求欧盟不要先发制人。在此问题上，马克龙此前曾更为激进。根据新建议，遭到来自中国或美国的经济攻击时，欧盟将有权予以有控制的回击。以北约核战略为样板，欧盟将可以做出灵活应对。先是对市场准入进行部分限制，而全面市场禁入，则是升级链条中的最后一个选项。
 
德法两国的期望是，这款新型‘二次打击武器’就足以对中国产生足够的威慑，以至于他们不敢让局势进一步升级。同核威慑一样，设立这一武器的初衷也是永远不要启用这个武器。但问题却在于，欧盟这款武器的威慑力实在难以令人信服。因为无论欧盟市场对中国多么重要，中国都能承受得起被欧盟市场排除在外的代价。但中国如果切断欧洲人获取稀土的渠道，欧洲的生产线几天之内都会停止运作。只要欧洲人不改变这一现状，任何对等反制都只是无稽之谈。”

items.title: 为钱卖国？德国前情报局长被捕
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/为钱卖国？德国前情报局长被捕/a-79565862?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 曾经担任德国联邦情报局（BND)局长、现年80岁的汉宁（August Hanning）在家中被捕。罪名涉嫌出卖国家及其他间谍行为。此前媒体报道过，汉宁经济状况出现困境，高额退休金的部分被没收抵债。
items.content:
为钱卖国？德国前情报局长被捕
2026年10月6日
（德国之声中文网）据包括《明镜在线》、《法兰克福汇报》、《图片报》、WDR、NDR 以及《南德意志报》等多家德语媒体报道，前德国联邦情报局（BND）局长奥古斯特·汉宁（August Hanning）于 10 月 6 日清晨在其位于德国西部明斯特地区的住所被捕。《明镜在线》提供了详尽的逮捕时间线：上午 6 点 41 分，特警部队冲入汉宁的住宅；上午 8 点 58 分，汉宁被押上一辆黑色面包车并带离现场。
与此同时，警方在德国南部巴伐利亚州 Bad Tölz‑Wolfratshausen 也展开了类似行动，逮捕了前 BND 工作人员曼弗雷德·D.（Manfred D.）。汉宁于 1998‑2005 年担任 BND 局长，曼弗雷德曾是汉宁的办公室主任。汉宁退休后，曼弗雷德继续为多位后继局长服务，直至今年年初正式退休，可谓是情报局内部最核心的知情圈成员之一。
《法兰克福汇报》透露，两人被指控涉嫌泄露德国国家情报。指控称，曼弗雷德向汉宁提供机密文件，汉宁随后将这些信息出售给第三方。《法兰克福汇报》还补充，已掌握的情报显示，此次泄密案并未直接涉及俄罗斯。《图片报》则报道，检方指控曼弗雷德截至 2022 年 6 月已向早已退休的汉宁交付多达 2000 份标记为高度机密的内部文件。
因为欠债 所以卖国？
《图片报》进一步指出，退休后的汉宁主要从事顾问咨询工作，并在多家公司担任监事会兼职，均属高层职位。此前媒体曾曝光，汉宁因曾在一家波罗的海国家银行担任监事会理事而陷入经济困境。该银行经营不善且遭受蓄意破坏，最终宣告破产。时任监事会理事的汉宁以及同为理事、前北约秘书长拉斯穆森均被牵连进银行破产程序中，需对银行及客户的损失承担责任。此事迫使原本收入丰厚、财政无忧的汉宁陷入个人财政危机，部分退休金被迫上缴以抵债。
此次逮捕的导火索与一起备受关注的“母亲绑架亲生子女”案件有关。案件嫌疑人、汉堡女富商克里斯蒂娜·布洛克（Christina Block）因与前夫在子女抚养权上产生争执，雇人绑架自己年幼的两名子女并秘密送回德国，企图借此获取子女的“控制权”。审理过程中发现，布洛克涉嫌与前 BND 局长汉宁进行权钱交易，利用汉宁的人脉帮助她实现“表面绑架、实则获得抚养权”的目的。正因如此，汉堡检察机关去年对汉宁的住所和办公地点进行了搜查。多家媒体分析认为，10 月 6 日的突袭逮捕行动很可能与去年搜查中获取的、显示汉宁出售机密情报的证据有关。
据悉，曼弗雷德·D. 当天已被带至卡尔斯鲁厄法官面前，而汉宁则将在次日（10 月 7 日）接受审讯。

items.description: 2026年诺贝尔物理学奖授予比利时裔美国物理学家弗朗西斯·哈尔岑（Francis Halzen），以表彰他在建立观测站探测高能中微子以及研究其产生机制方面所做的开创性工作。
items.content:
比利时裔美国粒子物理学家哈尔岑获诺贝尔物理学奖
2026年10月6日
广告
（德国之声中文网）哈尔岑目前任职于美国威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校，多年来，他担任南极冰立方（IceCube ）中微子天文台首席研究员。
哈尔岑发现，南极的冰层可用于追踪中微子，而中微子能穿透地球和人体，不留痕迹。它们极少与物质发生相互作用，因此常被称为“幽灵粒子”。“冰立方”（IceCube）观测站收集中微子相互作用数据，为研究人员提供了关于高能中微子如何产生的信息，甚至可能揭示此前未知的宇宙现象。
瑞典皇家科学院的奥尔森（Eva Olsson）在宣布获奖者的新闻发布会上表示，“这些‘信使’带来了宇宙的信息。它们开启了通往遥远星系的大门，并向我们揭示恒星爆炸的过程。”
诺贝尔物理学奖委员会主席马克·皮尔斯（Mark Pearce）在一份声明中说道：“弗朗西斯·哈尔岑领导一支由研究人员和工程师组成的国际团队，为我们提供了一台非凡的工具。他的坚韧不拔和科学远见为一种新型天文学铺平了道路。”
据路透社报道，2014年美国《史密森尼》杂志（Smithsonian magazine）在颁发“独创性奖”（Ingenuity Awards）时，称哈尔岑为“中微子先生”，盛赞他的“惊人的实验开启了天文学的新时代”。该杂志甚至刊登了一篇讲述他生平的漫画，标题是《一位物理学家对宇宙的探索从南极开始》。
诺贝尔物理学奖由瑞典皇家科学院评选，奖金总额为1200万瑞典克朗（约合120万美元）。这是继周一公布生理学、医学奖之后，今年揭晓的第二个诺贝尔奖项。周三将公布化学奖得主。

items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/欧元兑美元降至低点-投资者抛售法国债券/a-79562893?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 欧元兑美元汇率降至17个月来低点。分析人士认为，这将加剧欧盟的高通胀。投资者担忧法国债券的稳定性。
items.content:
欧元兑美元降至低点 投资者抛售法国债券
2026年10月6日
（德国之声中文网）周一（10月5日），欧元兑美元汇率创下17个月来新低。投资者原本已对全球政府债券收益以及油价上升颇为忧虑，如今更加上对欧元区债券、特别是法国债券的担忧。
2026年以来，欧元兑美元大多处于下跌状态，相较年初下跌约5%。周一的汇率为1欧元兑换1.12美元，是2025年初以来的最低点。
对法国债券长期稳定性的疑虑增加，导致投资者上周加速抛售法国债券。
法国的财政问题由来已久。总统马克龙2017年5月上任后，大规模减税，公共开支攀升。
如今，法国债务占GDP的比重接近118%。该国仍不断推出不平衡的预算。其年度预算赤字如今经常超过5%。马克龙上任前，这一比例为3.4%。
更青睐德国债券？
不少投资者转向被视为更安全的选项，如德国政府债券。
上周，法国与德国政府10年期债券的收益差距达到欧元区债务危机以来的最高水平。这一指标是衡量欧盟财政稳定性的重要指数。
外界因此呼吁欧洲央行采取措施，避免对法国债券的忧虑演变成恐慌。德意志银行分析师里德（Jim Reid）周一表示，他预期政治决策者将继续关注美元与欧元汇率的趋势，但目前不会采取干预市场的措施。
经济和政治压力都给市场带来不确定性。就法国的情况而言，外界担心2027年大选中右翼的勒庞当选总统。而在德国，民粹政党AfD崛起也引发类似的忧虑。
牛津经济研究院领衔的欧元区经济师阿马罗（Ricardo Amaro）向DW表示，欧元走弱可能加剧通胀问题。“欧元进一步疲弱可能会加剧通胀，而高通胀原本就已预期会持续到2027年。”
欧元走弱可能会增加进口商品的成本，特别是以美元计价。全球大宗商品如石油、天然气以美元计价，这意味着能源价格或将继续飙升，美国进口商品也是如此。

items.title: Three arrested after raid on gang accused of helping migrants pretend to be gay to get asylum
items.description: Those targeted by Home Office immigration enforcement officers are accused of charging migrants up to £4,500 for fabricated evidence.
items.content:
Three arrested after raid on gang accused of helping migrants pretend to be gay to get asylum
- Published
Immigration enforcement have made arrests in connection with a suspected criminal network believed to be behind dozens of fake asylum claims from people pretending to be gay.
It follows a BBC investigation earlier this year, which revealed that law firms and advisers were helping migrants pose as gay in an effort to get asylum.
Those targeted by Home Office immigration enforcement officers this morning are accused of charging migrants up to £4,500 for fabricated evidence, including staged photographs and fake documents.
They are thought to have aided dozens of asylum claims from Bangladeshi men, claiming they would be in fear for their lives if they returned home.
Two people were arrested at addresses in London this morning on suspicion of fraud and immigration offences, with Home Office officers also seizing phones, jewellery and thousands of pounds in cash. A third person was arrested on suspicion of being in the country illegally.
Chris Foster, a regional lead for criminal investigations at the Home Office, said the fake claims were connected to a Bangladeshi community LGBT organisation called Apanjon, which is based in Whitechapel, east London.
He said asylum caseworkers had initially spotted patterns in suspicious claims, which raised concerns about the group, and that immigration officers had been investigating for several months.
"We've got some intelligence that they can provide fake letters and documents, and they could charge anywhere between £1,000 and £4,500," Foster said.
"It could be letters of support from Apanjon, it could be staged photographs, suggesting that these people are gay, it could be letters from people claiming to be in a friendship or a sexual relationship - [a] same-sex relationship - as the claimants."
More than 100 asylum claims linked to the criminal network are being reviewed by the Home Office. Foster said some of the fake asylum applications would have "undoubtedly" been granted.
Immigration judges have previously criticised evidence from Apanjon as unreliable or not credible and found that an applicant who claimed to have attended the group's events had submitted staged photographs.
The Home Office said the group would often vouch for men who claimed asylum on the basis they were gay only after having initially been refused on political grounds. In one case, a man didn't raise his sexuality until nine years after his original claim.
The group is accused of using the same tactics as those pushed by advisers exposed in the BBC's investigation earlier this year.
A Home Office spokesperson said it was continuing to review asylum claims linked to that reporting, which led to two arrests in May.
In the BBC report, published in April, an adviser called Tanisa Khan told an undercover reporter she could provide a "comprehensive package", including photographs at gay clubs and other supporting evidence.
She was linked to a community group called Worcester LGBT, which she told the reporter they should attend in order to add to evidence for his fake claim.
Men attending one of the group's events at a community centre in Beckton, east London, claimed they were not really gay. One said: "Nobody is a gay here. Not even 1% are gay. Not even 0.01% are gay."
The investigation also revealed how bogus medical conditions and fake news websites were being used to bolster fraudulent asylum claims.
Worcester LGBT has since closed. Its founder previously said the group did not create or support fabricated evidence in asylum claims and it was not up to the organisation to determine whether any individual was actually gay.
Khan blamed communication difficulties for a "misunderstanding" and denied advising the reporter to make a false claim or offering to create fabricated evidence.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said "those faking persecution are beneath contempt and mock real victims who need protection".
"To the gangs profiting from this disgraceful fraud: you will be prosecuted, stripped of your dirty money and shut down," she said.
"And to those cheating the system, your claim will be thrown out, and you will be removed from this country."
A conviction for asylum fraud carries a maximum sentence of up to 10 years in prison.

items.title: Tear gas in Paris and Marseille as school protests grow across France
items.description: Crowds of mainly teenagers called for more resources for schools and an end to what they called police repression.
items.content:
Tear gas in Paris and Marseille as school protests grow across France
- Published
Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France, as a wave of protests by high-school pupils spread to their parents, university students and unions.
Crowds of teenagers marched from the Place de la République in Paris, calling for more resources for schools, and what they called less repression from police.
Police clashed with demonstrators in Lyon, used tear gas in Paris and Marseille and water cannon in Rennes, but there was little of the serious trouble that marred previous protests.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the earlier violence and said since the protests had begun 215 students and 85 staff had been hurt as well as 715 police officers.
The government said there had been disruption in 891 high schools on Tuesday - almost a quarter of all lycées - and said more than 250,000 demonstrators had taken to the streets during the day.
Students' unions put the number at 450,000, and said the number of high schools blockaded was 1,800 on what the protesters dubbed "Act Three" of their movement.
In Marseille, thousands of demonstrators moved around this city, stopping momentarily to chant before moving on as police changed direction.
A group of masked protesters grabbed bollards and bins and tried to barricade themselves off from police. Riot officers fired tear gas, and the protesters dispersed.
"Most of us aren't violent," said Alissa, a student in Marseille. "We're going to the streets because they've closed our schools... schools are falling apart."
Her friend, Sacha, said the ceilings in Marseille's schools were leaking and conditions were generally rather poor, "so we can't really work a lot of time". "We will keep doing this until good measures are taken," he added.
In parliament, the prime minister accused the radical-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of seeking to "sow chaos" ahead of presidential elections in seven months' time.
President Emmanuel Macron is nearing the end of his second and final term in office and LFI leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon is currently runner-up in the opinion polls behind Marine Le Pen of the hard-right National Rally.
Macron was due to chair a meeting with ministers at the Élysée Palace on Tuesday evening to assess the situation.
Education Minister Édouard Geffray said that from the start he had appealed for dialogue rather than school blockades and complained that "ultra-violent elements infiltrated the high-school student movements".
He is now under pressure to respond to the students' demands. What has been offered, including a website for students to express their grievances and an afternoon of internal discussion in schools on Friday, has made little impression so far.
There seems little chance of the protests coming to an end just yet. France's biggest union, the CGT, has said that further protests involving school and university students are being planned for Thursday.
There is widespread concern over allegations of "disproportionate force" by police, and France's IGPN police inspectorate has been investigating a number of cases.
One police officer who fired a tear-gas grenade at a high school student at Saint-Ouen-l'Aumône, north-west of Paris, last week has now been charged by prosecutors with "violence... resulting in mutilation or permanent disability".
Eden, 14, was part of a group blockading the Château d'Épluches lycée for 15-18-year-olds when he was hit in the face. His lawyer said he suffered a fractured jaw, and that his upper teeth were broken and four of his lower teeth were gone.
On Monday, a 15-year-old's hand was torn off after a so-called anti-encirclement grenade was fired in unclear circumstances near a school in the northern city of Lens.
Authorities say he picked up the "sting ball" grenade which then exploded, but students allege he was hit directly after an officer fired.
The grenade is considered a non-lethal weapon and the local prefect has said the incident took place when police were confronted by a group of 200-250 students throwing stones and fireworks.
What began with local anger at overcrowded classrooms, a lack of teaching staff and dilapidated school buildings in the northern Paris suburb of Seine-Saint-Denis in mid-September has since spread across the country, and extended to some universities too.
Late on Tuesday, the French interior ministry said a total of 6,547 had been stopped or arrested by police since 28 September.
Tuesday's protests drew people of all ages. One couple in their 70s, Alain and Michèle, joined the march in central Paris, to show their support for young students, explaining that as former teachers they understood the problems that France's education system was facing.
"We are the grandparents of three students who are all mobilised. They have protested peacefully in front of their respective high schools in Paris in recent days, but they were still tear-gassed," Alain told the BBC, his voice trembling.
Additional reporting by Manon Prat in Paris.

items.title: British national arrested in connection with RAF Fairford incident
items.description: It is the seventh arrest in connection to the incident near RAF Fairford last month.
items.content:
British national arrested in connection with RAF Fairford incident
- Published
A 22-year-old British national has been arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident close to RAF Fairford, counter-terror police said.
He was arrested in Westminster, London, on Tuesday as part of the investigation into the incident near the airbase in Gloucestershire on 27 September.
It is the seventh arrest in connection to the incident but no one has been charged.
A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase.
Senior national coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, Vicki Evans, said it "remains a live investigation" and police are continuing to "pursue multiple lines of enquiry".
Five men were arrested on 27 September near the base in connection with the incident and were subsequently released on police bail.
The men, aged between 23 and 25, were detained in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base.
They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".
A sixth man, a 25-year-old dual Iranian-British national, was arrested on 1 October in Westminster and was also later released on bail.
RAF Fairford, near the village of Whelford, has been used by the US Air Force for decades.
In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base to the Middle East, after the UK approved a request for Fairford to be used for defensive strikes against Iran.
On Sunday, it emerged the US had pulled its bombers out of the base and returned them to America.
US President Donald Trump said the aircraft were removed due to "some threats" to the base without giving specific details.
While speaking to a group of reporters outside the White House on Monday, Trump was asked if a "specific threat" had led the US to pull its bombers from the airbase.
He replied: "Yeah I think we can say that. They didn't fly out by accident.
"There were some threats. And rather than tempting the enemy, we'll capture the enemy and beat the enemy.
"But why should we leave them there? So we moved them around a little bit. Not very far."
Earlier, US Vice-President JD Vance said the bombers were moved "out of an abundance of caution".
The comments came after US media reports suggested the decision was made after intelligence suggested Iran was plotting a drone attack. The BBC has not verified those reports.
On Tuesday, a spokesperson for US European Command, which coordinated American military activity in Europe, said it would be "inappropriate to discuss matters of intelligence" but that the US would "continue to assess the threat environment" at bases.
The spokesperson added the US remains at the "highest state of readiness" and would take "appropriate actions to protect our people, our platforms, and the bases where our forces operate".
Prior to Trump's intervention on Monday, a No 10 spokesperson had insisted RAF Fairford was safe and pointed to his previous comments, where he praised the UK's "police, defence and security services" in relation to the base.

items.title: Asos confirms hackers sent 'unauthorised' notification to app users
items.description: Asos confirmed an "unauthorised customer notification" was sent out via its app on Tuesday, after users raised alarm.
items.content:
Asos confirms hackers sent 'unauthorised' notification to app users
- Published
Asos says it is investigating "unauthorised activity" involving third-party platforms it uses after customers received a notification from its app sent by hackers.
Dozens of people told the BBC they received the strange "ASOS HACKED" message from the clothing and beauty store's app on Tuesday morning - with some saying it left them "scared" to open the app.
The notification was addressed to the company's data protection officer and IT teams in what cyber security experts said looked like a "brazen" extortion attempt.
Asos acknowledged the "unauthorised customer notification" on Tuesday afternoon, saying some "basic personal information" may have been accessed.
In an email to customers on Tuesday night, the company apologised and urged customers not to engage with the notification. And it said the website and app are "operating as usual" promising customers they can "shop with confidence" while it investigates the incident.
The company has not as of yet informed the UK's data watchdog, the Information Commission's Office (ICO), about any breach.
Exactly how many Asos customers received the notification on Tuesday remains unclear, but Google's Play store says the ASOS app has been downloaded to android devices more than 10 million times.
The British retailer has a substantial global footprint - serving around 17 million customers each year across more than 150 markets.
Some Asos app users in Australia, France, Sweden and the Republic of Ireland had also received the notification, according to local reports on Tuesday.
Hackers seeking to pile pressure on potential victims by informing their customers is rare, as most extortions happen in private, so this incident may go down as a significant moment in cyber-attack history.
Shares in the company fell by around a tenth on Tuesday.
Charlotte Wilson, head of enterprise at cyber-security firm Check Point, called it a "deeply serious" and "brazen" attack whereby the hackers had apparently "turned Asos' own app into their ransom note".
But she told the BBC that Asos customers should not be "scared and frightened" - encouraging those worried to change their passwords, avoid clicking on the notification's link and be cautious about possible scam emails or texts.
- What can I do to protect myself after 'Asos hacked' message? 
  - Published1 hour ago
Extortion message
Users of the Asos app appeared to have received the alarming notification at around 10:00 BST on Tuesday.
Headlined "ASOS HACKED" and addressed to the company's data protection officer and IT teams, it said: "We have fully compromised the Snowflake instance."
"Engage with us, or we will leak it," it added, before linking to a Telegram channel.
The message left many ASOS customers confused.
"At first I thought it was an ad or a fun promotion like 'ASOS HACKED get 50% off everything for a limited time only'," Jodie, an analyst from Edinburgh, told the BBC.
"Then I read the rest of the message which clearly showed that it wasn't an ad and instead a message to IT."
"My main concern is that my information, such as bank information, home address, telephone number, has been compromised," said Erin, a student at the University of Sheffield.
She told the BBC that while her friends have expressed similar concerns about a potential data leak, her sister did not receive the notification on the Asos app.
"So the question is what is the extent? Are all customers affected even if they didn't get the notification? It's poor from Asos on all fronts."
Asos said in its statement that it took "immediate action to restrict access to the notification platforms" on Tuesday - adding it was working with specialists within and outside the company, as well as relevant authorities.
It said it does not believe payment-card information or account passwords were impacted, and that its site and app are "operating as normal".
"Customer trust is incredibly important to us, and if the situation changes an update will be provided as appropriate," it said.
The BBC understands the National Cyber Security Centre has offered assistance to Asos.
Meanwhile Snowflake - whose tools are used by dozens of firms to collect, analyse and store data - told the BBC its investigation was ongoing, but it had so far found "no compromise" of its platform.
The company's services have, however, been the subject of many high profile data breaches in recent years.
According to cybersecurity expert Jen Ellis, Snowflake collects data from multiple sources for analysis, and an "enormous" firm like Asos will have lots of data about how people shop globally.
However Dan Bird, from cybersecurity firm Horizon3, said the message implied the apparent hackers' access had gone beyond the Snowflake database.
"Sending a push notification to Asos's app users would require access to the company's notification system, which is separate from the Snowflake data platform the attackers claim to have compromised," he said.
"If both claims hold up, it suggests the attackers got hold of credentials that opened more than one door."
What can I do to protect myself?
The company has also shared a statement, external to the London Stock Exchange's Regulatory News Service, which provides updates to investors.
Cybersecurity experts, including Ellis, have told the BBC those behind those behind this incident are most likely trying to "apply pressure" to Asos to meet their demands, rather than target its customers.
While those who received this notification will undoubtedly be concerned, it is important to know that it does not mean your phone has been hacked.
We are still waiting to find out exactly what "basic personal information" may have been impacted in this incident, if any.
But for now, the advice is:
- Do not click on links in the notification
- Visit Asos's official website directly for updates
- Watch out for emails, texts or calls offering refunds, compensation or help with your account - scammers will exploit this type of incident when they know people are worried
- Try and use different passwords for your online services
- Enable two-step verification on email and banking accounts
- Keep an eye on your online transactions for anything unusual

Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment
1:18
What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.
Link Copied!
Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.

Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”

The former president met with attorneys at Trump Tower on the eve of his arraignment
From CNN's Kristen Holmes
From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.
(Reuters/Getty Images)
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Trump is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

Photos: Trump arrives in New York City a day before his expected arraignment
From CNN's Photo Desk
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.

Former president poised to huddle with advisers at Trump Tower
From Jeff Zeleny
A supporter of former President Donald Trump holds a "Trump Won" sign outside of Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Alex Kent/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.

Special counsel has secured evidence of how Trump handled classified records at Mar-a-Lago, sources say
From CNN's Katelyn Polantz and Evan Perez
Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.
The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say. That includes prosecutors pursuing evidence of Trump’s intent to keep classified records after he left the White House, plus his knowledge that the records remained in his possession after the Justice Department demanded their return last May.
Witnesses are being questioned about what they saw in Trump’s private residential and work areas within the club, some of the sources said.
